properties.decision:
UNDECIDED as a vocabulary question, but MUCH SMALLER than it looked, and the skill that tests it is BUILT (2026-07-25, the brainstorm skill). REFRAMED by Anthony the same day, and the reframe was the useful part: what he and his brother were asking for is not a staging GATE, it is a KIND. "I think I now realize what my brother's idea was trying to say — it is like a brainstorming session where you can work through ideas without committing to anything yet. These would be more like 'ideas' not yet fleshed out and could be held in the graph as just that, 'brainstorming ideas'." That dissolves the contradiction this decision was opened over: the git study rejected the index because a gate between every edit and the graph is where intent goes to be forgotten, whereas a brainstorm is the opposite move — the idea DOES enter the graph, immediately, labelled as what it is. Nothing waits outside, so nothing is lost, and the design still never claims a half-formed thought as intent. THE FINDING THAT SHRANK THE QUESTION, from reading the detector while building the skill: the existing vocabulary ALREADY tells a musing from a choice, and a computation already reads the difference. `detect_gaps` raises `undecided_decision_point` only on a proposed Decision holding TWO OR MORE REGISTERED ALTERNATIVES — a fork with a real design export behind each branch (detect.rs: `alts.len() < 2 { continue }`). A proposed Decision whose options live in its prose therefore raises NO gap at all. So brainstormed ideas are silent by construction, and the nudge to choose arrives exactly when the ideas stop being ideas: register_alternative turns an option into a fork, and being asked to decide a fork is correct. Nobody has to remember which is which, and no label was needed to get it. WHAT A `brainstorm` KIND WOULD STILL BUY, and it is now a short list rather than the four-item one recorded yesterday: (a) delivery and certainty counts already exclude Decisions, so nothing is owed there; (b) gap silence is already delivered, per the finding above; (c) what remains is RETIREMENT — an idea nobody has touched in months could be surfaced as a candidate for tidying rather than sitting in the decision list forever, which is a real computation and the only one left standing; and (d) READABILITY — a person scanning 70-odd Decisions cannot tell at a glance which were choices and which were musings, which the skill currently answers with a sentence of prose inside the node rather than with a queryable property. PRIOR FRAMING, KEPT because it was true when written: the ask read as an opt-in "think first, commit later" mode; a session making no write calls IS rubber-ducking and the read tools are the ducking aids; and the narrow question was what happens at the END — which the skill now answers as a PROMOTION step, not a commit step.

=====================================================================
ADDED 2026-08-10 — THE CAPABILITY HALF, AND IT IS NOT SILENT.
Anthony re-opened this by asking, of 34 stuck gaps: "what a not-yet-agreed
wish should be in this graph?" RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.
=====================================================================

THE FINDING ABOVE HOLDS FOR DECISIONS AND FAILS FOR CAPABILITIES. "Silent by
construction" rests on detect.rs skipping a proposed Decision with fewer than two
REGISTERED alternatives. Nothing analogous protects a Capability: one at `planned`
with no Requirement behind it raises `unmotivated_capability`, with no Artifact
`unrealized_capability`, with no Verification `unverified_capability`. THREE GAPS
EACH, FOREVER, BY CONSTRUCTION.

MEASURED 2026-08-10: 34 of 73 open gaps — 47% — are the [BL-nnn] rows, and they
have sat unanswerable since 2026-08-07. The cost of the wrong home for a wish is
not theoretical; it is half the gap list.

⭐ TWO ACCEPTED DECISIONS COLLIDE HERE AND NEITHER KNEW IT. `dec:backlog-is-retired`
routes unbuilt work to "a Capability at `planned` BEHIND A REQUIREMENT". Read
strictly it is coherent — the Requirement is what makes the Capability motivated.
But the migration wrote the Capability half and not the Requirement half, and the
reason it did is the interesting part: A BACKLOG ROW USUALLY HAS NO REQUIREMENT
TO WRITE. "Advanced testing tiers" is a wish nobody has agreed to; inventing a
Requirement to motivate it would manufacture intent, which is precisely what this
project forbids everywhere else.

⇒ SO THE ROUTING IS NOT WRONG, IT IS INCOMPLETE FOR A SUBSET: work somebody
INTENDS is a Capability behind a Requirement; a wish nobody has agreed to has no
home, and got the Capability anyway.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) FINISH THE PRESCRIBED SHAPE — write the missing Requirements. Counter: for most
of the 34 there is no requirement anybody stated, so this manufactures intent to
silence a detector, and `graph_report`'s certainty line would count 18 new
`asserted` requirements nobody confirmed.

(b) A CAPABILITY GAINS A `proposed` STATUS. Requirement status models the INTENT
lifecycle (proposed / accepted / deferred / dropped / met); Capability status models
the BUILD lifecycle (planned / in_progress / realized / verified) and has no way to
say "wished for, not agreed". Adding it lets the detectors stay quiet honestly.
⭐ THIS IS THE SAME ROOT AS `dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state`,
already open and ALREADY ASSIGNED TO ANTHONY — that one asks for the other end of
the same missing axis. They should be decided together or one will foreclose the
other. Counter: it MOVES THE SCHEMA STAMP, and two statuses on one type meaning
two different lifecycles is a modelling smell in itself.

(c) A WISH IS NOT A CAPABILITY AT ALL. Route it to a `proposed` Decision — which
IS silent by construction, per this node's own finding — phrased as "should we
build X?". Cheapest by far and needs no schema change. Counter: a Decision is a
CHOICE somebody faces, and "advanced testing tiers" is not a choice, it is an item;
collapsing wishes into decisions makes the decision pile the backlog again, which
is the thing Anthony already said is unwieldy at 85.

(d) DROP THEM. If nobody has agreed to a wish in the months it has sat there, the
honest record may be that it is not wanted. Counter: `dec:bl-155` measured that
reflow2 cannot tell "unused" from "unreachable", and the same applies to a wish
nobody has looked at — dropping on silence deletes exactly what was never surfaced.

(e) ACKNOWLEDGE EACH, INDIVIDUALLY AND HONESTLY. The tool already refuses the lazy
form: `acknowledge_gaps` demands a reason PER GAP because "a batch under one shared
reason is exactly the erosion the ask-don't-repair rule exists to prevent". Counter,
and it is why this node exists rather than 34 acknowledgements: acknowledging is
treating the symptom. The detector is correctly reporting that a wish is wearing
the wrong type.

WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION: 34 acknowledgements sharing one rationale with the subject
swapped. That satisfies the letter of the tool's contract and defeats its purpose.

THE QUESTION THIS ACTUALLY TURNS ON, and it is the one to put to the user: DOES A
NOT-YET-AGREED WISH BELONG IN THE DESIGN AT ALL? If yes, it needs a home that is
silent until somebody agrees to it — (b) or (c). If no, the backlog was retired
into the wrong place and (d) is the honest answer for most of the 34.
properties.name: OPEN — do half-formed ideas get a place in the graph, distinct from things the design asserts?
properties.rationale: Raised by Anthony and his brother 2026-07-24, reframed by Anthony 2026-07-25, and the skill built the same day on his word ("go ahead with the brainstorm skill"). Built as a SKILL and not a schema change deliberately: it tests the practice at the cost of prose, and if the practice sticks the vocabulary question can be answered with evidence instead of taste — whereas a new node type or an enum value would have bought an upgrade doc and a foundation-migration checklist for a noun nobody had used yet. The evidence for the feature is this session itself: Anthony produced four isolation ideas he explicitly did not want to commit to, and the only home for them was a proposed Decision. That worked (dec:concurrent-work-isolation), which is why this is not urgent; it is also a slightly wrong fit, since a Decision node is meant for a choice someone is actually facing, and knowing exactly which part of the fit is wrong is what the finding above now pins down. Left PROPOSED because two of the four original arguments for a kind have dissolved and the remaining two (retirement candidates, at-a-glance readability) are real but small — and whether they are worth a schema change is Anthony's call, not a judgement to be made by the agent that just wrote the skill.
